To visualize the problem, I imagine a cube with a sphere inside it, such that the sphere touches the center of each face of the cube.
This means that the diameter of the sphere is equal to the side length of the cube.
Since the radius of the sphere is 3 inches, the diameter is 6 inches, and so is the side length of the cube.
The volume of the cube is the side length cubed, so it is 6^3 = 216 cubic inches.
To find how much metal was removed from the corners, I need to subtract the volume of the sphere from the volume of the cube.
The volume of the sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr^3, where r is the radius.
Plugging in r = 3, I get V = (4/3)π(3^3) = 36π cubic inches.
Subtracting this from the volume of the cube, I get 216 - 36π cubic inches.
This is the final answer, since the problem does not ask me to simplify or approximate it.
Final answer: 216 - 36π cubic inches
